description: From the rooftop terrace of the Torre Tavira, 45 metres above the old town, Cádiz spreads out in a sea of white rooftops and mirador watchtowers under the moon. The cathedral's golden dome rises in the distance, warm windows glow here and there below, and the dark Atlantic rims the horizon with the city's lights beyond. The tower — the port's official watchtower since 1778 and home to Spain's first camera obscura — gives the best panoramic viewpoint in the city, and on a clear 24°C night it feels like standing over a luminous map of three thousand years.
